You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To obtain your fbi file, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Research the specific FOIA request requirements for the Department of Justice (1 hour)
Step 2. Print out the completed Form-361 Privacy Act Request (5 minutes)
Step 3. Draft a detailed cover letter explaining the scope of your request (2 hours)
Step 4. Buy a box of envelopes for mailing (15 minutes)
Step 5. Locate a high-resolution scanner (30 minutes)
Step 6. Scan a backup copy of your entire physical application packet (10 minutes)
Step 7. Purchase a certified mail stamp with tracking (10 minutes)
Step 8. Research the current mailing address for the FBI Record Information Dissemination Section (20 minutes)
Step 9. Receive the final digital or physical file in the mail (8 weeks)
Step 10. Label a physical folder for your records (5 minutes)
Step 11. Download the standard FOIPA Request Form (10 minutes)
Step 12. Photocopy your birth certificate (5 minutes)
Step 13. Obtain a list of your previous residential addresses for the last 10 years (1 hour)
Step 14. Find a local notary public (45 minutes)
Step 15. Verify that all signatures match your government ID (10 minutes)
Step 16. Double-check the DOJ website for any recent procedural updates (30 minutes)
Step 17. Assemble all gathered documents into a single stack (15 minutes)
Step 18. Sign the certification of identity in the presence of a witness (10 minutes)
Step 19. Save a digital PDF copy of the request to your hard drive (5 minutes)
Step 20. Confirm the recipient's office hours for delivery (10 minutes)
Step 21. Review the cover letter for any typos or missing dates (30 minutes)
Step 22. Have the notary public stamp your identity verification form (15 minutes)
Step 23. Check your printer ink levels (2 minutes)
Step 24. Read through the FOIA exemptions list (45 minutes)
Step 25. Place the documents into the mailing envelope (2 minutes)
Step 26. Make a copy of your driver's license (5 minutes)
Step 27. Type out your full name and social security number on the form (20 minutes)
Step 28. Affix the correct postage to the envelope (5 minutes)
Step 29. Check the balance on your debit card for processing fees (2 minutes)
Step 30. Locate your old employment history records (3 hours)
Step 31. Write your return address on the top left of the envelope (2 minutes)
Step 32. Wait for the initial acknowledgment letter from the FBI (3 weeks)
Step 33. Create an online account on the FOIA.gov portal (15 minutes)
Step 34. Find your social security card (1 hour)
Step 35. Set up a calendar alert to check status in 30 days (5 minutes)
Step 36. Clear a space on your desk to organize paperwork (20 minutes)
Step 37. Finalize the date range for the records you are seeking (40 minutes)
Step 38. Gather all necessary personal identification documents (1 hour)
Step 39. Purchase a blue ink pen for official signatures (10 minutes)
Step 40. Fill in the "Subject of Request" section on the form (15 minutes)
Step 41. Research the Freedom of Information Act statutes (4 hours)
Step 42. Gather your old passports and travel records (2 hours)
Step 43. Walk to the nearest post office (20 minutes)
Step 44. Proofread the entire application packet (1 hour)
Step 45. Enter your contact information into the digital portal (15 minutes)
Step 46. Compile a list of any aliases or maiden names used (30 minutes)
Step 47. Hand the envelope to the postal clerk (2 minutes)
Step 48. File the postal receipt in a safe place (5 minutes)
Step 49. Check your internet connection (1 minute)
Step 50. Verify the legal definitions of "expedited processing" (1 hour)
